SHAPE — Hero Slider

Empowering Universities to Shape Smarter Cities

SHAPE strengthens higher education institutions in East Africa by developing innovative curricula, building academic capacity, and fostering international collaboration to prepare the next generation of smart city leaders.

Learn More

Driving Innovation for Inclusive and Sustainable Urban Development

Through education, research, artificial intelligence, open data, and innovation, SHAPE supports the development of resilient, people-centered, and sustainable smart cities across Kenya, Somalia, and Uganda.

Explore Our Activities

Connecting Europe and East Africa for a Smarter Future

SHAPE brings together nine universities and regional stakeholders to promote knowledge exchange, strengthen institutional capacity, and establish a sustainable EU–East Africa Smart City Alliance.

Meet Our Partners
SHAPE — Quick Facts (Flip Cards, White)

Quick Facts

An Erasmus+ Capacity Building initiative connecting European and East African universities to advance smart, sustainable city development.

Hover a card — or tap on mobile — to see more

Nine universities, coordinated by Moi University, pairing European technical expertise with East African context.

content.rendered:
SHAPE — Work Packages

Work Packages

Five coordinated Work Packages carry SHAPE from research through to a lasting EU–East Africa alliance.

Work Package 1

Project Management & Coordination Activities

Oversees day-to-day coordination, quality assurance, and reporting to keep SHAPE on schedule and aligned across every partner institution.

Lead Moi University
Work Package 2

Establishing Design Requirements for Smart Cities in Sub-Saharan Africa

Assesses regional needs and educational gaps to shape a strategic roadmap for a smart city curriculum built for East Africa's realities.

Lead Open University of Kenya
Work Package 3

Building a New Educational Curriculum for Smart Cities

Develops and pilots new Master's-level courses, open online learning, and trainer programmes spanning smart city disciplines.

Lead Kampala International University
Work Package 4

Implementation of Smart City Acceleration & Open Innovation Programme

Establishes Open Innovation Labs and hackathons, and launches the EU–East Africa Smart City Alliance, turning research into practice.

Lead University of Tartu
Work Package 5

Dissemination, Exploitation, Sustainability & Communication

Builds SHAPE's public presence and long-term sustainability through communication strategy, outreach, and digital channels.

Lead Mogadishu University

SHAPE — About

About SHAPE

The Smart City Higher Education Advancement Program in East Africa (SHAPE) is an Erasmus+ Capacity Building in Higher Education initiative designed to address the growing shortage of smart city skills across East Africa, particularly in Kenya, Somalia, and Uganda. Rapid urbanization in the region has created increasing demand for professionals capable of planning, designing, and managing smart, sustainable, and inclusive cities. However, higher education institutions currently lack specialized curricula, qualified academic staff, practical training facilities, and strong collaboration with industry and public institutions.

SHAPE responds to these challenges by modernizing higher education through innovative curricula, academic capacity building, digital learning, research collaboration, and open innovation. The project combines the technical expertise of European universities with the contextual knowledge of East African institutions to develop educational programmes that reflect the realities and priorities of African cities rather than replicating models developed elsewhere.

The project will introduce new Master's level courses and micro-credentials covering key smart city domains, including Artificial Intelligence, Open Data, Smart Mobility, Smart Energy, Smart Health, Community Engagement, and Sustainable Urban Development. Academic staff will receive specialized training, while universities will establish Open Innovation Labs to promote entrepreneurship, applied research, hackathons, and collaboration with industry and government.

Beyond curriculum development, SHAPE aims to create lasting partnerships between universities, municipalities, industry, civil society, and policymakers through a new EU–East Africa Smart Cities Alliance. By strengthening higher education institutions and producing highly skilled graduates, the project contributes to sustainable economic growth, digital transformation, and resilient urban development throughout East Africa. The initiative also aligns closely with the EU Global Gateway Strategy, supporting digital innovation, green transition, sustainable transport, and inclusive governance across Sub-Saharan Africa.

AI & Open Data
Smart Mobility
Open Innovation Labs

Our Goal

To strengthen higher education institutions in East Africa by developing innovative academic programmes, practical innovation ecosystems, and skilled graduates capable of designing, implementing, and sustaining smart, inclusive, and sustainable cities across Kenya, Somalia, and Uganda.

Our Mission

To modernize higher education through innovative curricula, digital technologies, industry collaboration, and capacity building that empower universities to produce professionals with the knowledge, skills, and leadership needed to drive sustainable smart city development in East Africa.

Learn More About SHAPE
SHAPE — Thematic Areas

Thematic Areas

SHAPE's curricula and Open Innovation Labs span twelve interconnected domains shaping the future of smart, sustainable cities.

Smart Cities & Sustainable Urban Development

Artificial Intelligence & Data-Driven Decision Making

Open Data & Digital Governance

Smart Energy & Renewable Energy Systems

Smart Mobility & Intelligent Transport Systems

Smart Health & Digital Healthcare

Internet of Things (IoT) & Sensor Technologies

Community Engagement & Citizen Participation

Innovation & Entrepreneurship

Digital Transformation in Higher Education

Open Innovation Labs & Hackathons

Capacity Building & Curriculum Development

SHAPE — Target Groups

Target Groups

SHAPE's impact reaches every part of the smart city ecosystem — from classrooms to city halls.

Universities & HEIs in Kenya, Somalia & Uganda Academic Staff, Researchers & Administrators Undergraduate & Postgraduate Students Government Institutions & Municipalities Smart City Practitioners & Urban Planners Technology Companies & Innovation Hubs Entrepreneurs & Startups Civil Society Organizations Local Communities in Urban Development Public & Private Sector Stakeholders
SHAPE — Expected Project Impacts

Expected Project Impacts

What success looks like when SHAPE reaches the end of its three-year journey — for institutions, graduates, and the region.

01

New Accredited Curricula

New accredited smart city curricula and micro-credential programmes introduced across partner universities.

02

Stronger Academic Staff

Academic staff equipped with modern teaching methodologies and advanced smart city competencies.

03

Open Innovation Labs

Open Innovation Labs established within East African universities to promote innovation, entrepreneurship, and applied research.

04

Deeper Collaboration

Stronger collaboration between universities, governments, industry, and local communities in addressing urban development challenges.

05

Employable Graduates

Enhanced digital, technical, and entrepreneurial skills among students and graduates, improving employability and regional economic growth.

06

International Collaboration

Increased international collaboration through virtual exchanges, joint research, and knowledge sharing between European and East African institutions.

07

A Lasting Alliance

A sustainable EU–East Africa Smart Cities Alliance established to continue collaboration beyond the project's lifetime.

08

Long-Term Regional Impact

Long-term contribution to inclusive, resilient, and sustainable smart city development across East Africa through higher education transformation.
